io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.endpoint_probe: tools/list on the source harness (2026-11-10, pre-deploy) -> 25 tools, protocol 2025-11-25, 3 resources, 4 prompts. Paid conformance 2026-08-18 on the deployed fingerprint: 686 assertions, 0 failed.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.long_description: Source-backed intelligence on the SAP AI & analytics services market (Joule, BDC, Datasphere, SAC, BW/4HANA, Databricks), read-only apart from two subscriber actions, so an assistant can answer precisely and cite the exact record. TWENTY-FIVE tools: FIFTEEN public and unauthenticated, plus TEN a subscriber key opens (listed, refusing by name, never hidden). Start with find_answers: a natural question in English, French or German is matched to twelve ranked challenges (agents in production, Joule value, the BW 7.5 cliff, BDC vs Datasphere vs Databricks…) and answered with what shipped, what is announced and the page to cite. Public tools: a directory of SAP consulting, recruitment and vendor organisations searchable by country, region, kind and declared SAP module, a profile per firm and an aggregate count; a published day-rate aggregate by country, specialisation and seniority — small, all secondary sources, each row in its own currency; a contract and job radar of public SAP analytics postings — filter it by employment_type, because it is mostly PERMANENT roles; what is gated there is a FIELD, not a row: the verified link to the original listing is a paid deliverable, every other fact stays public; a curated market-news corpus, each item carrying the upstream publisher's URL alongside ours; a concept encyclopaedia; the SAP module taxonomy; the metadata of the deep-research studies; the CV/profile platforms a consultant can sign up on; the Academy catalogue; and a traversal of the learning knowledge graph. The fifteen public tools need no credential; the ten paid ones (the full concept card, a study body, an Academy module, firm intelligence, the SAP end-customer corpus and profiles, an expansion brief, partner candidates, and two ACTIONS: submit_brief (a private SAP need) and request_introduction (its anonymised selection, an introduction the consultant accepts in the app; nothing e-mailed)) need the MCP Pass (€29.90/month or €299/year, analyticslegends.ai/mcp-server/) or a Firm Pass seat key; the Consultant and Legend web plans do not include MCP access. A key on a FREE account gets a small daily taste of the paid tranche (the number is in analytics-legends://tranche). Without a key the reference vocabularies (modules, firm kinds, platforms) come in full and the other public tools serve their first page (at most 10 rows) with the true match count; a free key pages. Every read tool is annotated readOnlyHint and every corpus row carries a citation_url. Retrieval with attribution is permitted, training is not. DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED at any tier: the opportunity-to-consultant matchers, and people — no tool returns anyone's identity or contact details.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.monitoring: Handshake, a real tools/call with data, and latency. Two watchers: a 20-minute tick on the maintainer's workstation (only while awake), and a cloud backstop twice a day calling tools/list AND a data-returning tools/call. Health: https://analyticslegends.ai/api/mcp-health.json — read its generated_at, do not assume a cadence.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.repository_scope: This repository is the server's PUBLIC FACE — manifest, descriptor, client config, docs. It carries no server code (the application repository is private: paid corpus, personal data). tools/list against the endpoint is the authority for the surface.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.tools_served: 25 on this endpoint: 15 public and unauthenticated, 10 gated and refused by name without a key on the MCP Pass or a Firm Pass seat. The MCP Pass opens all ten.
